# The core move of 2026-11-28: old path to new path

Mojolearn keeps the shared core small: code that one release family uses lives in that family (AGENTS.md part 4,
"A release rebuilds and re-records only the families that changed"). `tools/ops/move_core_files.py` moves the
files below out of `core/` and rewrites the references to them; `tools/ops/core_move_map.tsv` is its input and
holds one row for every file of `core/`, with the reason a file stays.

Permanent records are never rewritten: `docs/TOMBSTONES.md`, `docs/apple-fast/EXPERIMENTS.md`, the restore
patches, `verification/records/`, inline TOMBSTONE markers and dated notes under `docs/` keep the old paths.
To apply an old patch or follow an old note, replace the old path with the new one from this table. The module
name follows the path: `from core.forest_entry import ...` is now `from ensemble.forest_entry import ...`.

The family is the release family of `bindings/release_families.json` whose bindings are the only ones that
reach the file through imports.

## Deleted

| Old path | Why |
| --- | --- |
| `core/classical_ridge_impl.mojo` | 10 lines, no importer, no TOMBSTONE marker, not an experiment; named only by historical verification/records |

## What stays in core, and why

- Files that two or more families reach (the map names one binding per family as the proof).
- Files only the shared bindings reach: they are the core.
- `core/experiment_guards_<family>.mojo` and `core/classical_identical_controls/`: the rule file and the grid
  controls name those paths.
- Standalone check programs that `pixi.toml` runs against a kernel that stays.

The map marks a staying file `SPLIT CANDIDATE` when one family would be its only user once the
`_mojolearn_runtime_*_host` bindings stop importing it through the shared doors in `bindings/` and
`providers/python/`. Those are import cuts, not moves, and are not part of this table.
